parole.testo: From Middle Dutch geule, from two possible origins (which may have merged): * from Old French goule (“mouth”), and/or * from Old Dutch *gulja (as in the hydronym Geul, attested in 10th-century Latin as Gulia), of Proto-Germanic origin; perhaps cognate with Swedish göl.
Borrowed from Old French hoel or hael, diminutive from hoe (“hoe, mattock”), which is itself derived from Old Dutch houwan (“to hew”).
